in_text_mentions: ary ketones. The urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio was elevated at 112.01 mg/g (normal <30 mg/g). Nerve conduction studies indicated peripheral neuropathy in the right upper limb and both lower limbs. Visual acuity was 0.6 in the right eye and 0.04 in the left eye, with bilateral cataracts observed. CT imaging of the upper abdomen revealed irregular, bead-like dilatation of the pancreatic duct along with marked atrophy and calcification (Figure 2c). Similar imaging findings, although varying in severity, were observed in the proband’s mother and her second and third sisters (Figures 2b,e,g).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI shows a round cystic lesion consistent with a pancreatic pseudocyst, a complication explicitly linked to hereditary pancreatitis in the article title and in-text description. B: MRCP demonstrates numerous small cysts on the ventral pancreatic body, identified in the text as pancreatic pseudocysts occurring in the context of hereditary pancreatitis. C: T2-weighted MRI shows classic manifestations of hereditary pancreatitis including intraductal stones (defects), main pancreatic duct dilatation, and parenchymal thinning/atrophy.
panels.attribution_text: Fujiwara. Diagnosis of Hereditary Pancreatitis Following the Initial Acute Episode With Multiple Pseudocyst Complications.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.73653. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Abdominal MRI and MRCP findings Axial contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (A) shows a round cystic lesion with homogenous fluid density and a well-defined wall (arrows). MRCP (B) shows numerous small cysts on the ventral side of the pancreatic body (circles). T2-weighted MRI (C) shows defects in the main pancreatic duct (arrows), as well as dilatation of the main pancreatic duct and thinning of the pancreatic parenchyma. MRI: magnetic resonance imaging; MRCP: magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography
